column3: D'Addario Kaplan Solutions cello strings, model KS510 4/4M; the A3, D3 and C2 strings of a set of nominally identical strings, effective open-string length taken as 690 mm
column4: Tension, mass per unit length and bending stiffness EI as printed in the string-property table of Mansour, Woodhouse and Scavone, Enhanced wave-based modelling of musical strings, Part 1: Plucked strings (author manuscript Table 1, and the same rows in Mansour's McGill thesis, Table 2.1, printed p. 38); loss coefficients eta_F and eta_B from the same rows; strings mounted on a rigid granite base so that the Q factors reflect intrinsic damping only
column5: Values are as printed there; the printed loss rows are fitted to averaged Q factors of seven sets (the Q factors came from D'Addario); the eta_A air row of that table is not used because the renderer computes air drag from the diameter

column3: Outer diameters of the A, D and C strings of one lab cello (cello-I of ten instruments, a 1997 Canadian instrument) whose strings were of unknown make (the thesis says no information about the strings was accessible, the instruments had been owned for at least a year and strings were not changed regularly)
column4: Photographs of each string beside a ruler, counted in pixels; the diameters of cello-I and of one violin were checked against a Vernier calliper and the photographs; Percival 2013 (University of Glasgow PhD thesis), Table 3.2, printed p. 69; the thesis states the diameters are believed accurate to 10 percent
column5: These strings are NOT the Kaplan strings of the other observation: the diameter is that of an unnamed lab-cello string, paired here with the Kaplan tension, mass and stiffness as a stated approximation; Table 3.2 prints one value per string and does not say which method gave it
